title: Algorithm coverage: reconcile the stale gap beads and make the RustCrypto set the default
description:
Two halves: correct the record, then act on the decision that every RustCrypto algorithm should be available everywhere, with sane errors where a regulator forbids one.

STALE BEADS TO RECONCILE
PKIX-77k9.1 (P1), PKIX-gphz (P2) and PKIX-qws.1/.2/.3 all describe RSA-PSS, Ed25519 and ECDSA P-521 as missing. They are implemented. pkix-path/src/verifiers.rs dispatches all three:
  - OID_RSASSA_PSS (verifiers.rs:74, used at :304, :399, :505)
  - OID_ED25519 (:90, used at :537)
  - OID_SECP521R1 (:59, dispatched at :213)
and the rustcrypto umbrella feature is rsa + p256 + p384 + p521 + ed25519 (pkix-path/Cargo.toml:38). PKIX-qws.4 (legacy SHA-1) is NOT stale and should not be actioned: SHA-1 is refused by design.

So 77k9.1 is a P1 describing a past state -- the same pattern the 46-P1 review-epic audit kept finding. It should be closed or rewritten to the remaining work below, not worked as filed.

THE DECISION (2026-11-25)
Assume everything in RustCrypto is available everywhere. Callers should not have to opt into ordinary modern algorithms.

That is not what the defaults do today: pkix-path has default = ["rsa", "p256"]. A plain dependency gets RSA and P-256 only -- no P-384, no P-521, no Ed25519, no RSA-PSS. Those arrive only via the rustcrypto feature, which pkix-chain re-exposes as its own rustcrypto feature and pkix-ct enables directly.

Work: make the full RustCrypto set the default in pkix-path, and follow the change up through pkix-chain. Note this ADDS dependencies for every consumer rather than changing API -- a weight decision, not a semver one -- so it wants a deliberate call on whether the slimmer set stays available as an opt-out.

REGULATED ENVIRONMENTS
The mechanism already behaves correctly and should be preserved, not redesigned. An algorithm that is not compiled in returns VerificationError::unsupported_algorithm(), and an unavailable curve returns unsupported_key() (verifiers.rs:205, :214) -- distinct from MalformedKey, so a caller can tell 'this build does not do that' from 'that key is broken'. Nothing panics and nothing silently succeeds.

What to confirm rather than assume: that those errors stay legible at the pkix-chain boundary, so a FIPS deployment that meets a P-521 or Ed25519 certificate gets an error naming the algorithm rather than a bare path failure. Worth a test per excluded algorithm with the corresponding feature off.

INCIDENTAL
pkix-difftest/Cargo.toml:34 and :40 both describe the umbrella as 'rsa + p256 + p384', predating p521 and ed25519 joining it. Stale comments, worth correcting with the above.
